title: Wolf and Ember
premise: In the memoryless valley of Hollowmere, Silas Yarrow survives by stealing recollections from travelers who cross its border and selling them back to the desperate. When a dying courier presses a map of the Ember Road into his hands, Silas learns the covenant that keeps magic out of the valley is failing—and the memories he's stolen all these years contain fragments of the ritual needed to reforge it. Hunted by the Ashen Court, which wants the covenant broken so it can rule both realms, Silas must journey beyond the only home he's ever known, guided by a stranger's ghost-memory and a disgraced court scribe named Wren. At the Ember Forge, Silas discovers the covenant demands a willing sacrifice of one's own remembered life; instead of paying with his own past, he shatters the covenant entirely, scattering magic freely across both realms and destroying the Court's monopoly on power. He returns to Hollowmere with no memories of his own thefts—only Wren, who remembers for him.
about_author: Paloma Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging forgotten letters in a mountain library before turning to fiction. She writes about memory, borders, and the people history chooses not to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Silas Yarrow lifts a merchant's memory of the sea—a thing he's never seen—and sells it to a grieving widow. POV: Silas. The beat establishes his hollow competence and the ache beneath it: a man rich in other people's pasts, starving for his own.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Borderline
chapters.summary: A bleeding courier collapses at the valley's edge, pressing a scorched map into Silas's hands and whispering 'the Forge remembers' before dying. POV: Silas. Fear and reluctant curiosity war as Silas realizes the map shows roads beyond Hollowmere—roads he swore never to take.

chapters.title: What the Stolen Memories Whisper
chapters.summary: Examining his hoard of stolen memories, Silas finds recurring fragments: a forge, an oath, a woman's voice reciting covenant-words. POV: Silas. The emotional beat is vertigo—the discovery that his petty crimes have made him, unknowingly, the archive of something sacred.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Fell
chapters.summary: Wren, a disgraced Ashen Court scribe, tracks Silas into the valley and offers alliance: she knows the ritual, he holds its pieces. POV: Wren. Her chapter reveals the Court's corruption—covenant-breakers branded traitors—and her bitter resolve after watching them execute her mentor.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Silas crosses the border for the first time; sensation floods him—color too bright, grief too sharp—as ambient magic touches his mind. POV: Silas. Overwhelm and wonder give way to terror when an Ashen hunter's mark burns itself onto the map, meaning they can now find him anywhere.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: On the Ember Road, Silas steals a memory to save Wren from a toll-warden, breaking his own rule never to steal outside necessity. POV: alternating. Trust tentatively builds between them, but Silas hides that the stolen memory showed Wren betraying someone at the Forge.

chapters.title: The Court's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Ashen hunters ambush them at a river shrine; Wren reveals her hidden rank to buy their escape, and Silas learns the Court plans to sacrifice an entire city to fuel the broken covenant for themselves. POV: Wren. Guilt and fury fuse into purpose—the stakes turn personal and moral.

chapters.title: The Forge Remembers
chapters.summary: At the Ember Forge, the ghost-memory of the dying courier manifests and explains the price: the covenant reforges only through a willingly surrendered remembered life. POV: Silas. Facing erasure, Silas finally understands what his victims felt—and chooses anyway, while Wren secretly prepares a different answer.

chapters.title: Ember and Ash
chapters.summary: Climax: the Ashen Court arrives to seize the Forge; Wren turns her scribe-knowledge against her former masters, unbinding their authority, while Silas does the unthinkable—he feeds the Forge not surrender but release, shattering the covenant so magic belongs to no one. POV: alternating. Sacrifice without erasure; power dispersed rather than transferred.

chapters.title: The Man Who Gave His Thefts Away
chapters.summary: Silas returns to Hollowmere, his stolen memories dissolved into the world, remembering almost nothing of himself—but Wren stays beside him, telling him his own story each morning until new ones grow. POV: Silas. Quiet resolution: justice achieved not by law or sacrifice, but by refusing to let anyone own what lives in every mind.
